# About native-ce

native-ce is an event-authoritative, portable SQLite knowledge store. Authored changes append to authoritative logs and project into queryable state; the connected portable database is the caller's working boundary and content authority.

The engine supports multiple authenticated members. It can run through Native hosting or as a self-hosted binary. A hosted deployment may keep a catalog locator or control-plane object for the database, but that object does not replace the portable SQLite file as the content authority.

## Tool discovery

The normal executor surface derives its catalogue from executable operation contracts. Its discovery surface is currently not user-configurable, and it does not read account exposure profiles or family/tool overrides.

The legacy direct-tool surface retains `complete`, `focused`, and custom exposure preferences only as an internal compatibility and emergency-rollback seam, not as a supported user-facing setting. Those legacy filters are intentionally lossy: a hidden tool can be undiscoverable to the agent, and a visible workflow can refer to a dependency that the filter hides. Filtering affects discovery rather than authorization: a hidden legacy direct tool remains callable by exact name when the caller already knows it, filtering never grants permission, and every call still applies its normal authorization rules. Internal focused/core classification is inventory metadata, not a client-visible MCP recommendation field.

Use `bootstrap` for bounded caller-relative session context. Use `read_guide` when cross-cutting engine knowledge is needed; use the live tool schemas and responses for tool-specific contracts and recovery instructions.
